# Storefront UX Checklist: Storefront UX (Task 4)

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality review gate for the storefront UX spec before planning
**Created**: 2026-09-29
**Feature**: specs/008-storefront-ux/spec.md

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 - Are identity-block requirements specified for every listed element (name, logo/cover, status, description, contact) including missing-asset behavior? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK002 - Are category navigation requirements specified for active state, position retention, and cart preservation? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK003 - Are product-card requirements specified for price context, imagery, and availability states? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK004 - Are cart requirements specified for items, quantities, fees, totals, and controls? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK005 - Are pickup/delivery requirements specified for selection clarity, total updates, and gated fields? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK006 - Are search requirements specified for scope, matching fields, and empty states on every storefront? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK007 - Is "together at the top" for the identity block defined with a testable ordering or grouping rule? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK008 - Is "unmistakable" closed-state presentation defined with observable criteria? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK009 - Is "obvious" category switching defined with measurable navigation properties? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK010 - Is "simple and obvious" cart behavior defined with specific visibility and control criteria? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK011 - Is "graceful omission" for missing assets defined per element rather than as a general principle? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK012 - Can "minimal friction" from the UX principle be objectively verified against the acceptance scenarios? [Measurability, Spec §UX principle]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK013 - Are currency presentation requirements consistent between cards, cart, totals, and confirmation steps? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK014 - Are availability requirements consistent between product cards and checkout gating (no silent adds)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK015 - Are RTL and English requirements consistent across identity, navigation, cart, and totals? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK016 - Is the search-everywhere clarification consistent between FR-004 and the Constraints reuse statement? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK017 - Can SC-003 first-screen visibility be objectively verified across businesses with missing assets? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK018 - Can SC-004 zero-orderable-unavailable be tested across all listed input paths? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK019 - Can SC-005 total-equality be verified at each listed step (cart, toggle, confirmation)? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK020 - Can SC-006 keyboard and scaling criteria be verified without implementation knowledge? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK021 - Are SC-001 time bounds scoped with defined start and end points? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-001]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK022 - Are primary-flow requirements defined for the full visit-to-tracking journey? [Coverage, Spec §US1]
- [ ] CHK023 - Are alternate-flow requirements defined for delivery-disabled and closed/outside-hours businesses? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK024 - Are exception-flow requirements defined for offline, slow-connection, and empty-menu states? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK025 - Are recovery requirements defined for cart preservation across navigation, search, and connection loss? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK026 - Are requirements defined for rapid repeated input (double-tap, key repeat) on add-to-cart controls? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK027 - Are requirements defined for logo/cover image load failure? [Edge Case, Gap]
- [ ] CHK028 - Are requirements defined for keyboard traps and focus order in the checkout overlay? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-010]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK029 - Are weak-device performance requirements specified with concrete asset and animation limits? [Completeness, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK030 - Are touch-target and text-scaling requirements quantified with measurable thresholds? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK031 - Are live-region requirements specified for cart and total updates? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK032 - Are security non-regression requirements specified for the refined storefront? [Completeness, Spec §Constraints]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK033 - Is the no-API-change assumption validated against every presented field (identity, currency, availability)? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK034 - Are out-of-scope boundaries explicit for variants, pre-orders, accounts, loyalty, and animation? [Completeness, Spec §Constraints]
- [ ] CHK035 - Is the visual-identity preservation criterion specified with a verifiable boundary for refinements? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit.implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit.specify` and `/speckit.clarify`
- Focus: flows and presentation, accessibility and RTL, performance and scope (reviewer, rigorous gate)
- 100% of items carry traceability references; no implementation-behavior assertions included
